name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch
  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they ar…

But there's a subtlety in the codex idle stall message: previously `providerIdleStallFired(response, idle)` used the raw global; now idle is tuned — good.

7. The `matchesForUrl` sort: `matches.sort` is not stable in Dart? Dart's List.sort IS stable (guaranteed since Dart 2.12? Actually Dart docs say List.sort is NOT stable... Let me recall: Dart's `List.sort` documentation says "The sort is stable"? Checking memory: `List.sort` — "Sorts this list according to the order specified by the compare function. The compare function must act as a Comparator. A Comparator may compare objects as equal (return 0), even if they are distinct objects. Sorting is stable, meaning the relative order of equal elements is preserved." Yes, Dart's List.sort is stable. But they compare registration index `b.$2.compareTo(a.$2)` so ties fully broken anyway — with equal base URLs, depth equal, index distinct. So deterministic regardless.

8. Seed-order change: customModels before customProviders — AC3.

9. AC4 claim: "every untouched config resolves byte-identically". But the seed-order fix changes resolution for existing configs declaring timeouts on BOTH customProviders and models.custom for the same endpoint — the review round 1 noted this as migration-facing (the author acknowledged; AC3 says intended). Hmm, wait — actually there's a subtle question: does the ORIGINAL gh-1398 semantics (pre-PR) for equal depth "later registration wins"? Old `forUrl` used `>=` so later registration wins at equal depth. Old seed order was customProviders first, then customModels, then roleRefs, then queue. So before this PR, for the same endpoint at same depth, models.custom won over customProviders (registered later). After the PR, seed order swapped: models.custom first, customProviders later → customProviders wins. This is a behavior change for existing configs! The AC3 says "the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom" — i.e., the claim is the designed precedence is role > customProviders > models.custom, so this is intentional. But AC4 says "every untouched config resolves byte-identically". These contradict for configs with both surfaces on the same endpoint. The author acknowledges in the review reply ("seed-order fix changes resolution for existing configs... intended per AC3, but migration-facing"). So it's a documented intended change but it's arguably a backward-compat break not flagged in changelog. Suggestion-level.

- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they ar…

blocks.text:
- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

347:  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
1935:  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

blocks.text:
+      '---
name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch
  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.

blocks.text:
- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config

when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they ar…

blocks.text:
- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.

68:#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
347:  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
1935:  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch
  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they ar…

- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  SHARED FAST GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL   ║
# ║  loc ≤ 2800 lines (crap4dart) · analyze · tests · coverage ≥ 80% ·        ║
# ║  duplication < 1% (flutter_app < 3.7%) · cross-module < 0.31%             ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# THE shared fast gate used by BOTH the pre-commit hook and CI (issue #177,
# AC7). Both callers run this exact script and diff the one-line markers
#   GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>
# for hook/CI parity. Every known stage ALWAYS prints exactly one marker:
# OK when it ran and passed, SKIP <reason> when it was not selected or a
# required tool is missing. A failing stage aborts the script with exit 1
# BEFORE its OK marker is printed (marker absent = failed).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh [--scope auto|all|core|app|docs] [--stages list] [--hook]
#
#   --scope auto  Derive the scope from changed paths (default):
#                 - in a git hook (--hook flag or GIT_INDEX_FILE set):
#                   staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only`;
#                 - in CI (BASE_REF + HEAD_REF env vars set):
#                   `git diff --name-only $BASE_REF...$HEAD_REF`;
#                 - otherwise: "all" (safe default).
#   --scope all   Run every stage.
#   --scope core  analyze + test-core + coverage + crap + dup + dupx.
#   --scope app   analyze + dup + dupx + flutter.
#   --scope docs  analyze only.
#   --stages l    Comma-separated stage list; overrides the scope-derived set.
#                 Known stages: analyze,test-core,coverage,crap,dup,dupx,flutter,integration-mock
#
#
# Path rules (union logic, E1; test/** counts as core, E6):
#   docs/ | *.md | prompts/ .................. analyze
#   lib/ | bin/ | test/ | pubspec.* .......... + test-core, coverage, crap, dup, dupx
#   test/integration/** ...................... + integration-mock (no-key legs,
#                                              MockLlmServer; issue #551)
#   flutter_app/ | packages/ ................. + dup, dupx, flutter
#   scripts/ | .github/ | crap4dart.yaml ..... ALL stages (safe default, E2)
#   anything unknown ......................... ALL stages (safe default)
#
# Concurrency overrides: FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY / FA_FLUTTER_TEST_CONCURRENCY
# (auto-throttled via detect_test_concurrency, same as scripts/pre-commit).
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N makes the integration-mock
# stage rerun ONLY its failed files, up to N times, before failing — the
# load-sensitive PTY/grid timing legs stop costing a full 2.5 h leg per
# ambient flake (default 0 = single-shot, behaviour unchanged).
#
# CRAP ratchet scoping: in --hook mode the analyze runs over the STAGED
# lib/bin files only — the ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a
# pre-existing offender in an untouched file cannot block an unrelated
# commit. Non-hook runs (and ci.yml's whole-repo `crap4dart analyze`)
# keep the full-repo view, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
