blocks.text:
- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per

In seeding, registration order: models.custom, customProviders, roleRefs, queue. `matchesForUrl` sorts depth desc, then registration index desc. Wait — DEPTH takes priority over registration order! So an entry with a LONGER base path at a LOWER surface beats a higher surface with a shorter base path. E.g. models.custom entry with baseUrl `https://api.example.com/v1` vs customProviders with baseUrl `https://api.example.com` — the models.custom entry (depth deeper) wins even though customProviders is a higher precedence surface. Is that intended? The doc says "longest base path first; among equal depths the LAST registration first — the boot seeder registers low surfaces before high ones". So depth trumps surface height. That is a design decision (gh-1398 semantics kept: deepest base URL match wins). Consistent with old `forUrl` behavior which used depth first. OK.

blocks.text:
- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

68:#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
347:  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
1935:  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

While waiting, continue the code review. Remaining items:

1. Read remaining diffs: test/providers/provider_tuning_test.dart and provider_tuning_config_test.dart changes (partly seen in truncated diff), prompts.g.dart (single line change — seen: SKILL.md content +1 line, "providerTimeouts: # GLOBAL fallback").

2. Check `_matchesBaseUrl`/`_baseDepth` unchanged.

3. Review the `resolveProviderTimeouts` chain semantics vs `forName`/`forUrl` precedence: `name` first, then URL matches. Note `forName` returns entry by name; if `name` entry declares neither field, URL matches are consulted — fine.

4. Check stall-message classifier: `connectWatchdogTag` unchanged. The connect stall message now may include scope note — contains-matching classifiers OK per design.

5. Potential issue in `_sendWatchedOnce`: shadowing — the parameter is named `connectTimeout`, which shadows the top-level getter `connectTimeout` imported from provider_common? In provider_tuning.dart there's `providerConnectTimeout` etc. Within provider_common.dart itself, the top-level has getters `providerConnectTimeout`/`effectiveProviderConnectTimeout`. The named param `connectTimeout` is a new name — no conflict.

6. In `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` timeout message: `idle window ${_idleTimeout.inSeconds}s ($timeoutSource)` — hmm, `inSeconds` truncates sub-second windows (120ms → 0s). The codex test asserts bare text so no issue there; but in the loopback IT they use 1s. Minor: if someone sets 1500ms the stall line says "idle window 1s". Pre-existing pattern though (the old message also used inSeconds). Suggestion-level nit at most.

7. `sendProviderRequest` and `sendWatchedProviderRequest` got new named params — backwards compatible. `startProviderResponse` is the only caller passing them besides codex? Check other callers of sendWatchedProviderRequest (anthropic, google, openai_completions?) — they pass through startProviderResponse presumably. Fine.

8. Check AC2 claim: "customProviders entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table". The URL-keyed table works by baseUrl matching — resolution through the entry happens whenever request URL matches baseUrl. OK.

9. Precedence claim per AC3: "role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry > global > default". In seeding, registration order: models.custom, customProviders, roleRefs, queue. `matchesForUrl` sorts depth desc, then registration index desc. Wait — DEPTH takes priority over registration order! So an entry with a LONGER base path at a LOWER surface beats a higher surface with a shorter base path. E.g. models.custom entry with baseUrl `https://api.example.com/v1` vs customProviders with baseUrl `https://api.example.com` — the models.custom entry (depth deeper) wins even though customProviders is a higher precedence surface. Is that intended? The doc says "longest base path first; among equal depths the LAST registration first — the boot seeder registers low surfaces before high ones". So depth trumps surface height. That is a design decision (gh-1398 semantics kept: deepest base URL match wins). Consistent with old `forUrl` behavior which used depth first. OK.

10. Backward-compat AC4 vs seed-order swap: existing configs with both customProviders and models.custom timeouts on the same endpoint (same baseUrl → same depth) now resolve differently (customProviders wins instead of models.custom). Author acknowledged as intended per AC3. The doc in providers.md says "Configs without the keys behave byte-identically" — true, but configs with BOTH keys on the same endpoint at equal depth change behavior — contradicts "every untouched config resolves byte-identically". The changelog note suggestion was raised in review round 1 as a 💡. This is at most SUGGESTION (intended design change, documented precedence).

11. prompts.g.dart sync — verify: run scripts/gen_prompts.dart --check if possible.

12. The docs in models_config.dart (~L20) and custom_providers.dart (~L13) still document old precedence — the round-1 suggestion. Check current state.

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges

      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})

        run: |

blocks.text:
- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

blocks.text:
- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

68:#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
347:  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
1935:  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

1. Read remaining diffs: test/providers/provider_tuning_test.dart and provider_tuning_config_test.dart changes (partly seen in truncated diff), prompts.g.dart (single line change — seen: SKILL.md content +1 line, "providerTimeouts: # GLOBAL fallback").

2. Check `_matchesBaseUrl`/`_baseDepth` unchanged.

3. Review the `resolveProviderTimeouts` chain semantics vs `forName`/`forUrl` precedence: `name` first, then URL matches. Note `forName` returns entry by name; if `name` entry declares neither field, URL matches are consulted — fine.

4. Check stall-message classifier: `connectWatchdogTag` unchanged. The connect stall message now may include scope note — contains-matching classifiers OK per design.

5. Potential issue in `_sendWatchedOnce`: shadowing — the parameter is named `connectTimeout`, which shadows the top-level getter `connectTimeout` imported from provider_common? In provider_tuning.dart there's `providerConnectTimeout` etc. Within provider_common.dart itself, the top-level has getters `providerConnectTimeout`/`effectiveProviderConnectTimeout`. The named param `connectTimeout` is a new name — no conflict.

6. In `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` timeout message: `idle window ${_idleTimeout.inSeconds}s ($timeoutSource)` — hmm, `inSeconds` truncates sub-second windows (120ms → 0s). The codex test asserts bare text so no issue there; but in the loopback IT they use 1s. Minor: if someone sets 1500ms the stall line says "idle window 1s". Pre-existing pattern though (the old message also used inSeconds). Suggestion-level nit at most.

7. `sendProviderRequest` and `sendWatchedProviderRequest` got new named params — backwards compatible. `startProviderResponse` is the only caller passing them besides codex? Check other callers of sendWatchedProviderRequest (anthropic, google, openai_completions?) — they pass through startProviderResponse presumably. Fine.

8. Check AC2 claim: "customProviders entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table". The URL-keyed table works by baseUrl matching — resolution through the entry happens whenever request URL matches baseUrl. OK.

9. Precedence claim per AC3: "role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry > global > default". In seeding, registration order: models.custom, customProviders, roleRefs, queue. `matchesForUrl` sorts depth desc, then registration index desc. Wait — DEPTH takes priority over registration order! So an entry with a LONGER base path at a LOWER surface beats a higher surface with a shorter base path. E.g. models.custom entry with baseUrl `https://api.example.com/v1` vs customProviders with baseUrl `https://api.example.com` — the models.custom entry (depth deeper) wins even though customProviders is a higher precedence surface. Is that intended? The doc says "longest base path first; among equal depths the LAST registration first — the boot seeder registers low surfaces before high ones". So depth trumps surface height. That is a design decision (gh-1398 semantics kept: deepest base URL match wins). Consistent with old `forUrl` behavior which used depth first. OK.

10. Backward-compat AC4 vs seed-order swap: existing configs with both customProviders and models.custom timeouts on the same endpoint (same baseUrl → same depth) now resolve differently (customProviders wins instead of models.custom). Author acknowledged as intended per AC3. The doc in providers.md says "Configs without the keys behave byte-identically" — true, but configs with BOTH keys on the same endpoint at equal depth change behavior — contradicts "every untouched config resolves byte-identically". The changelog note suggestion was raised in review round 1 as a 💡. This is at most SUGGESTION (intended design change, documented precedence).

11. prompts.g.dart sync — verify: run scripts/gen_prompts.dart --check if possible.

12. The docs in models_config.dart (~L20) and custom_providers.dart (~L13) still document old precedence — the round-1 suggestion. Check current state.

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any

  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks

    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was

      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

- name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        # gh-1199 AC6: explicit file list (not the bare directory) so the
        # quarantine filter can drop flake-quarantined files here too.
        run: |
          targets=$(find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' | sort | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "integration-mock targets: $targets"
          dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty $targets

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: release-pending
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

While waiting, continue the code review. Remaining items:

1. Read remaining diffs: test/providers/provider_tuning_test.dart and provider_tuning_config_test.dart changes (partly seen in truncated diff), prompts.g.dart (single line change — seen: SKILL.md content +1 line, "providerTimeouts: # GLOBAL fallback").

2. Check `_matchesBaseUrl`/`_baseDepth` unchanged.

3. Review the `resolveProviderTimeouts` chain semantics vs `forName`/`forUrl` precedence: `name` first, then URL matches. Note `forName` returns entry by name; if `name` entry declares neither field, URL matches are consulted — fine.

4. Check stall-message classifier: `connectWatchdogTag` unchanged. The connect stall message now may include scope note — contains-matching classifiers OK per design.

5. Potential issue in `_sendWatchedOnce`: shadowing — the parameter is named `connectTimeout`, which shadows the top-level getter `connectTimeout` imported from provider_common? In provider_tuning.dart there's `providerConnectTimeout` etc. Within provider_common.dart itself, the top-level has getters `providerConnectTimeout`/`effectiveProviderConnectTimeout`. The named param `connectTimeout` is a new name — no conflict.

6. In `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` timeout message: `idle window ${_idleTimeout.inSeconds}s ($timeoutSource)` — hmm, `inSeconds` truncates sub-second windows (120ms → 0s). The codex test asserts bare text so no issue there; but in the loopback IT they use 1s. Minor: if someone sets 1500ms the stall line says "idle window 1s". Pre-existing pattern though (the old message also used inSeconds). Suggestion-level nit at most.

7. `sendProviderRequest` and `sendWatchedProviderRequest` got new named params — backwards compatible. `startProviderResponse` is the only caller passing them besides codex? Check other callers of sendWatchedProviderRequest (anthropic, google, openai_completions?) — they pass through startProviderResponse presumably. Fine.

8. Check AC2 claim: "customProviders entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table". The URL-keyed table works by baseUrl matching — resolution through the entry happens whenever request URL matches baseUrl. OK.

9. Precedence claim per AC3: "role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry > global > default". In seeding, registration order: models.custom, customProviders, roleRefs, queue. `matchesForUrl` sorts depth desc, then registration index desc. Wait — DEPTH takes priority over registration order! So an entry with a LONGER base path at a LOWER surface beats a higher surface with a shorter base path. E.g. models.custom entry with baseUrl `https://api.example.com/v1` vs customProviders with baseUrl `https://api.example.com` — the models.custom entry (depth deeper) wins even though customProviders is a higher precedence surface. Is that intended? The doc says "longest base path first; among equal depths the LAST registration first — the boot seeder registers low surfaces before high ones". So depth trumps surface height. That is a design decision (gh-1398 semantics kept: deepest base URL match wins). Consistent with old `forUrl` behavior which used depth first. OK.

10. Backward-compat AC4 vs seed-order swap: existing configs with both customProviders and models.custom timeouts on the same endpoint (same baseUrl → same depth) now resolve differently (customProviders wins instead of models.custom). Author acknowledged as intended per AC3. The doc in providers.md says "Configs without the keys behave byte-identically" — true, but configs with BOTH keys on the same endpoint at equal depth change behavior — contradicts "every untouched config resolves byte-identically". The changelog note suggestion was raised in review round 1 as a 💡. This is at most SUGGESTION (intended design change, documented precedence).

11. prompts.g.dart sync — verify: run scripts/gen_prompts.dart --check if possible.

12. The docs in models_config.dart (~L20) and custom_providers.dart (~L13) still document old precedence — the round-1 suggestion. Check current state.

    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

The implementation is identical to `_tunedIdleTimeout`. The problem must be in the test: MockClient.streaming's returned response has `request: null` because the test's `StreamedResponse` constructor doesn't pass `request:` and MockClient copies `response.request`.

Let me verify: in the test, `http.StreamedResponse(controller.stream, 200, headers: {...})` — no `request` param. MockClient.streaming wraps: `StreamedResponse(response.stream, response.statusCode, request: response.request, ...)` → request null. So `response.request?.url == null` → falls to global 300s → the test hangs until its own 10s `.timeout` → fails. That's the reproduction I saw: "TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000: Future not completed" at test line 330 — exactly the test's `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10))`.

Wait — but does the codex flow use `client.send(request)` where client is the MockClient? Yes. And in real IOClient, `request` is set. So production code is fine; the test is broken — it never exercises the tuned lookup because the mock strips the request.

Hmm wait, but let me double check — is that true? In package:http 1.6.0, `BaseClient.send`... MockClient overrides send entirely and returns the wrapped response with request: response.request (null). Yes.

Actually wait — let me check whether the test would pass by a different path: The codex session maybe uses `sendProviderRequest`? No — codex bypasses and uses its own send; the response comes from `_client.send(request)`.

So how did the author verify this test? They said dart VM SIGKILLed, static only. And CI on 7e6e794f4... thread shows the previous head 3b7d27be had "every check pass" but 7e6e794f4 (which added this test) — the CI run 38269584471 was on e5b1cf7d and failed shards. So this test has never been green in CI. This is a genuine BLOCKING: the new regression test fails — in CI shards 1/3 and hostile env, and probably quality gate... Actually why would the Quality gate fail? Maybe because quality gate runs the fast gate (analyze + targeted tests). Let me check what ci_fast_gate.sh runs. Maybe the codex test is in the fast gate set.

Fix for the test: pass `request:` in the StreamedResponse, e.g. capture the request in the handler:

```dart
http.StreamedResponse(
  controller.stream,
  200,
  request: request,
  headers: {...},
)
```

The MockClientStreamHandler signature is `(BaseRequest request, ByteStream bodyStream)`. So `request: request` works — it's a BaseRequest; StreamedResponse.request is BaseRequest? type. Yes.

# THE shared fast gate used by BOTH the pre-commit hook and CI (issue #177,
# AC7). Both callers run this exact script and diff the one-line markers
#   GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>

# OK when it ran and passed, SKIP <reason> when it was not selected or a
# required tool is missing. A failing stage aborts the script with exit 1
# BEFORE its OK marker is printed (marker absent = failed).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh [--scope auto|all|core|app|docs] [--stages list] [--hook]
#
#   --scope auto  Derive the scope from changed paths (default):
#                 - in a git hook (--hook flag or GIT_INDEX_FILE set):
#                   staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only`;
#                 - in CI (BASE_REF + HEAD_REF env vars set):
#                   `git diff --name-only $BASE_REF...$HEAD_REF`;
#                 - otherwise: "all" (safe default).
#   --scope all   Run every stage.
#   --scope core  analyze + test-core + coverage + crap + dup + dupx.
#   --scope app   analyze + dup + dupx + flutter.
#   --scope docs  analyze only.
#   --stages l    Comma-separated stage list; overrides the scope-derived set.
#                 Known stages: analyze,test-core,coverage,crap,dup,dupx,flutter,integration-mock
#
#
# Path rules (union logic, E1; test/** counts as core, E6):
#   docs/ | *.md | prompts/ .................. analyze

#                                              MockLlmServer; issue #551)
#   flutter_app/ | packages/ ................. + dup, dupx, flutter
#   scripts/ | .github/ | crap4dart.yaml ..... ALL stages (safe default, E2)

#

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

68:#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
347:  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
1935:  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

68:#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
347:  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
1935:  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
