68:#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
347:  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
1935:  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})

3. Review the `resolveProviderTimeouts` chain semantics vs `forName`/`forUrl` precedence: `name` first, then URL matches. Note `forName` returns entry by name; if `name` entry declares neither field, URL matches are consulted — fine.

4. Check stall-message classifier: `connectWatchdogTag` unchanged. The connect stall message now may include scope note — contains-matching classifiers OK per design.

5. Potential issue in `_sendWatchedOnce`: shadowing — the parameter is named `connectTimeout`, which shadows the top-level getter `connectTimeout` imported from provider_common? In provider_tuning.dart there's `providerConnectTimeout` etc. Within provider_common.dart itself, the top-level has getters `providerConnectTimeout`/`effectiveProviderConnectTimeout`. The named param `connectTimeout` is a new name — no conflict.

6. In `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` timeout message: `idle window ${_idleTimeout.inSeconds}s ($timeoutSource)` — hmm, `inSeconds` truncates sub-second windows (120ms → 0s). The codex test asserts bare text so no issue there; but in the loopback IT they use 1s. Minor: if someone sets 1500ms the stall line says "idle window 1s". Pre-existing pattern though (the old message also used inSeconds). Suggestion-level nit at most.

7. `sendProviderRequest` and `sendWatchedProviderRequest` got new named params — backwards compatible. `startProviderResponse` is the only caller passing them besides codex? Check other callers of sendWatchedProviderRequest (anthropic, google, openai_completions?) — they pass through startProviderResponse presumably. Fine.

8. Check AC2 claim: "customProviders entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table". The URL-keyed table works by baseUrl matching — resolution through the entry happens whenever request URL matches baseUrl. OK.

9. Precedence claim per AC3: "role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry > global > default". In seeding, registration order: models.custom, customProviders, roleRefs, queue. `matchesForUrl` sorts depth desc, then registration index desc. Wait — DEPTH takes priority over registration order! So an entry with a LONGER base path at a LOWER surface beats a higher surface with a shorter base path. E.g. models.custom entry with baseUrl `https://api.example.com/v1` vs customProviders with baseUrl `https://api.example.com` — the models.custom entry (depth deeper) wins even though customProviders is a higher precedence surface. Is that intended? The doc says "longest base path first; among equal depths the LAST registration first — the boot seeder registers low surfaces before high ones". So depth trumps surface height. That is a design decision (gh-1398 semantics kept: deepest base URL match wins). Consistent with old `forUrl` behavior which used depth first. OK.

10. Backward-compat AC4 vs seed-order swap: existing configs with both customProviders and models.custom timeouts on the same endpoint (same baseUrl → same depth) now resolve differently (customProviders wins instead of models.custom). # Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent

  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the

  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to

  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

```
+      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override
```


**Failure 2 (shard 3)** — `test/skills/fa_self_config_accuracy_test.dart` "every documented nested key is pinned and really parsed": the SKILL.md edit documents `roles.default.[].connectTimeoutMs`/`roles.default.[].streamIdleTimeoutMs` (and possibly customProviders/models.custom keys) but doesn't extend the test's `_nestedKeySources` pinned key map. Note the error names only `roles.default.[].*` — so customProviders/models.custom nested keys presumably were already pinned (from gh-1398), but the roles chain entry keys are new documentation.

Wait — were the roles entry timeout keys documented before this PR? The diff added the two lines to SKILL.md's roles example:
```
+      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override
+      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000  #   (slow local model recipe, see below)
```
So yes — the PR documents nested keys in SKILL.md and the accuracy test catches undocumented/unpinned nested keys. The fix: extend `_nestedKeySources` in the test (and verify roles_config parser reads them — it does).

**Shard 1 also has 3 ERRORs**: "AC14 d1/d2/tail: extension sendMail lands in the main fabric inbox / fabric mail reaches the extension service worker / extension mailbox appears in the fabric directory". # Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter
  picking the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` for parity with the
  terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by
  `result.json` presence (errored trials report as their own breakdown
  line; exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders the full
  report — table, errored breakdown, ledger row — to
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity). Both bench adapters export
  `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) into the
  agent session and audit the exact value. fa core: deadline awareness —

```
+      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override
```


9. `sendProviderRequest`/`sendWatchedProviderRequest` public API additive named params — backward compatible. Barrel re-exports unchanged.

10. Performance: `matchesForUrl` allocates + sorts per call... `forUrl` was already O(n); now O(n log n) + allocation per request (per send + per stream). n is tiny (handful of entries). Negligible.

Wait the original file has `import 'provider_common.dart';` LAST (unusual order) — pre-existing. 12. The codex test: `expect(message, isNot(contains('idle window')))` — asserts the endpoint-table window keeps bare text. OK.

13. In the codex test, `providerTimeoutsOverride = null;` then `addTearDown(providerTuningRegistry.clear);` — no addTearDown for providerTimeoutsOverride reset. They set it to null (default) — if a previous test in the file left a non-null override, this test's state is polluted... they set null, fine. Not restoring to previous is fine in practice.

14. Loopback test: uses `Model(...)` directly with streamIdleTimeout etc. — direct wire verification. Good.

15. provider_tuning_loopback_test third test asserts per-leg behavior — good coverage for the round-1 fix.

🚨 **BLOCKING: the new codex regression test hangs — CI red (Core tests shard 1/4, Hostile ambient env, Quality gate)**

Reproduced deterministically on head `e5b1cf7d` (also fails standalone): the test times out after its own 10s cap at `chatgpt_codex_test.dart:330`.

Root cause — the mock never delivers the request, so the tuned lookup this test exists to exercise never runs:

```dart
// test handler
return http.StreamedResponse(
  controller.stream,
  200,
  headers: {'content-type': 'text/event-stream'},
);
```

`MockClient.streaming` (package:http 1.6.0) forwards `request: response.request` — which is **null** here — so in `_consumeSseLines`:

```dart
final tunedIdle = response.request?.url == null      // always null with this mock
    ? effectiveProviderStreamIdleTimeout             // → 300s global
    : providerStreamIdleTimeoutForUrl(response.request!.url);
```

the 120ms entry window is silently skipped and the stream idles at the 300s global until the test's own `.timeout(Duration(seconds: 10))` trips. Production code is correct (real clients set `request`); the test is the defect — as written it never validates the fix it claims to pin.

Verified fix (test passes with it, ~10ms instead of 10s):

```dart
return http.StreamedResponse(
  controller.stream,
  200,
  request: request,
  headers: {'content-type': 'text/event-stream'},
);
```

Side benefit: without it the abandoned run leaves the 300s idle timer armed against a dead controller, which can fire into a later test in the file.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the tuning table is never seeded on the app surface — AC2's "both CLI and app" overclaims**

`seedProviderTuning` has exactly one production caller: `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (the CLI boot). `flutter_app/lib` contains no reference to `providerTuningRegistry`/`seedProviderTuning` (verified by grep, also on the merge head), so in the desktop app a `customProviders:` entry or a roles chain entry declaring `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` is silently ignored — the watchdogs keep the global/default windows. The URL-keyed table this PR builds is empty there.

This is a pre-existing gh-1398 gap (main seeds in the same single place), so nothing regressed — but this PR's AC2 states "boot seeding, both CLI and app", and the new docs/SKILL.md present the keys as config surfaces without noting the app limitation. A user who tunes a slow local model per the docs' recipe in the app gets a silent no-op, which is exactly the false-confidence class the stall-line naming was built to avoid.

Options:

1. Wire `seedProviderTuning(...)` into the app's boot path (`AgentService` init) — same data is already loaded there for provider/roles resolution.
2. Or correct the AC2 claim + add a one-line scope note to `docs/agents/providers.md` / SKILL.md ("timeout tuning applies to CLI sessions").

Either is fine; the silent mismatch between the claim and the shipped behavior is the part worth fixing before this lands.

```dart
final window = idle.inMilliseconds < 1000

    : '${idle.inSeconds}s';
```

Display-only; the watchdog itself runs the exact duration either way.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the tuning table is never seeded on the app surface — AC2's "both CLI and app" overclaims**

`seedProviderTuning` has exactly one production caller: `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (the CLI boot). `flutter_app/lib` contains no reference to `providerTuningRegistry`/`seedProviderTuning` (verified by grep, also on the merge head), so in the desktop app a `customProviders:` entry or a roles chain entry declaring `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` is silently ignored — the watchdogs keep the global/default windows. The URL-keyed table this PR builds is empty there.

This is a pre-existing gh-1398 gap (main seeds in the same single place), so nothing regressed — but this PR's AC2 states "boot seeding, both CLI and app", and the new docs/SKILL.md present the keys as config surfaces without noting the app limitation. A user who tunes a slow local model per the docs' recipe in the app gets a silent no-op, which is exactly the false-confidence class the stall-line naming was built to avoid.

Options:

1. Wire `seedProviderTuning(...)` into the app's boot path (`AgentService` init) — same data is already loaded there for provider/roles resolution.
2. Or correct the AC2 claim + add a one-line scope note to `docs/agents/providers.md` / SKILL.md ("timeout tuning applies to CLI sessions").

Either is fine; the silent mismatch between the claim and the shipped behavior is the part worth fixing before this lands.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: sub-second scoped windows render as `idle window 0s`**

`scopedNote` uses `${idle.inSeconds}s` — a model override like `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 250` (a legitimate choice for tests/edge endpoints) renders `idle window 0s (role x override)`, which reads as a broken note in the stall line.
```dart
final window = idle.inMilliseconds < 1000
    ? '${idle.inMilliseconds}ms'
    : '${idle.inSeconds}s';
```

Display-only; the watchdog itself runs the exact duration either way.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the tuning table is never seeded on the app surface — AC2's "both CLI and app" overclaims**

`seedProviderTuning` has exactly one production caller: `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (the CLI boot). `flutter_app/lib` contains no reference to `providerTuningRegistry`/`seedProviderTuning` (verified by grep, also on the merge head), so in the desktop app a `customProviders:` entry or a roles chain entry declaring `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` is silently ignored — the watchdogs keep the global/default windows. The URL-keyed table this PR builds is empty there.

This is a pre-existing gh-1398 gap (main seeds in the same single place), so nothing regressed — but this PR's AC2 states "boot seeding, both CLI and app", and the new docs/SKILL.md present the keys as config surfaces without noting the app limitation. A user who tunes a slow local model per the docs' recipe in the app gets a silent no-op, which is exactly the false-confidence class the stall-line naming was built to avoid.

Options:

1. Wire `seedProviderTuning(...)` into the app's boot path (`AgentService` init) — same data is already loaded there for provider/roles resolution.
2. Or correct the AC2 claim + add a one-line scope note to `docs/agents/providers.md` / SKILL.md ("timeout tuning applies to CLI sessions").

Either is fine; the silent mismatch between the claim and the shipped behavior is the part worth fixing before this lands.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: sub-second scoped windows render as `idle window 0s`**

`scopedNote` uses `${idle.inSeconds}s` — a model override like `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 250` (a legitimate choice for tests/edge endpoints) renders `idle window 0s (role x override)`, which reads as a broken note in the stall line. Same for `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator`'s `' — idle window ${_idleTimeout.inSeconds}s ($timeoutSource)'`.

Match the value's magnitude when formatting, e.g. show `inMilliseconds` under 1s:

```dart
final window = idle.inMilliseconds < 1000
    ? '${idle.inMilliseconds}ms'
    : '${idle.inSeconds}s';
```

Display-only; the watchdog itself runs the exact duration either way.
